description: FP8 GEMM dequantized per block: a fp32 scale per 1 x 128 of a (K-major or MN-major) and per 128 x 128 of b. aiter gemm_a8w8_blockscale (CK / asm / bpreshuffle), DeepSeek-style FP8 checkpoints.

fp8_dtype.doc: e4m3fn on gfx950, e4m3fnuz on gfx942 (harness_lib.regime_dtype decides; never hard-code)

scale_major.doc: a_scale is (m, scale_k) when K, (scale_k, m) when MN

hooks.preshuffle_16x16: (t, name, sym) -> aiter shuffle_weight(t, layout=(16, 16)) with t.is_shuffled = True, exactly as the model loader stores the weight.

call: Pass a, b, a_scale, b_scale (and the output dtype) as the live caller does; return out.

timing.cache: b and b_scale are weights (cold between layers in serving; read-evict matches); a/a_scale come from the preceding quant kernel and are L2-warm in deployment.

negative_controls: apply b_scale of block (j, kb+1) to block (j, kb): a wrong-scale error proportional to the scale ratio, far outside baseline_relative
skip the a_scale multiply on the last K block
pitfalls: Bound is baseline_relative, not dot_product: gfx950 FP8 MFMA accumulates below the IEEE fp32 model, so even the installed kernel violates a dot_product bound. The candidate may not be more than 2x the installed kernel's own error against float64.
Scales must be positive and log-uniform; scales from U(0,1) include near-zero blocks that hide a misapplied scale.
fnuz vs OCP e4m3: the same bit pattern is a different value. Build fp8 operands with harness_lib.regime_dtype for the arch the server runs.
The CK blockscale tuned CSV is keyed by (M, N, K); a candidate that changes the tile list must be timed per padded-M tier the decode buckets hit.
